headline: Azure secrets stolen, ScreenConnect hijacks, Iran-linked tanker attacks
overview: Attackers exploited a flaw in Microsoft's classic Azure API Management to reach stored secrets, with Norway tying it to energy-sector victims, so rotating credentials is the urgent step. Other major threats include a critical ScreenConnect bug that lets attackers hijack MSP technicians' machines and a possible Shiny Hunters revival that remains unconfirmed. Policy and leadership news and AI-related stories round out the day.

topStories.title: Azure API Management flaw exposes customer secrets
topStories.summary: Microsoft says a flaw in the classic tiers of Azure API Management let attackers reach stored keys and tokens on instances not configured to its best practices. Norway's energy sector found it first, and Microsoft's fix does not invalidate secrets already stolen, so customers should rotate them and check logs.

topStories.title: Iran-suspected cyberattacks on tankers and cargo ships
topStories.summary: US officials are investigating attacks on as many as 50 ships carrying oil, gas and chemicals, reportedly exploiting Fortinet router flaws, with some vessels receiving ransom or bomb threats. Attribution is unresolved, with Iran named as the prime suspect and Russia still considered, and a Trump administration official says there is no evidence yet of Iran's involvement.

topStories.title: Critical ScreenConnect flaw hijacks MSP technicians
topStories.summary: Attackers are exploiting a critical ScreenConnect bug that lets a malicious guest in a support session push and run a file on a technician's computer without warnings. Huntress tracked a campaign from October to November, and the fix is in version 26.6.5 or later.

topStories.title: Shiny Hunters claims a comeback with shaky proof
topStories.summary: A new leak site claims the Shiny Hunters group is back, signing posts with 2020-era PGP keys that were revoked in March. The keys are genuine but could have changed hands, so the link to the original group is unproven. Several recent arrests are mentioned, and none of the allegations have been tested in court.

topStories.title: Unpatched ASP.NET library under active attack
topStories.summary: A critical flaw in an old anti-CSRF library for ASP.NET web forms lets one unauthenticated request run code on the server. It is being exploited, the project has not been updated since 2008, and no patch is coming, so affected servers should remove the library.

topStories.title: Exposed databases leak billions of credentials
topStories.summary: Researchers found two unsecured databases holding billions of usernames, passwords, ID numbers and documents, largely from earlier breaches and infostealer malware. Both have since gone offline.

episodes.title: All hands on hack.
episodes.summary: Covers the Iran-linked tanker attacks, a possible Shiny Hunters return, a US bill for a CISA incident review board, a new national cyber director nominee, UK regulator warnings on AI agents, a South Korean utility data breach, and a Talos interview on prompt injection of AI assistants. Also reports a Bluetooth trailer brake vulnerability.

episodes.title: Iranian tanker hacks, Azure flaw exploited, espionage at OpenAI
episodes.summary: Covers the tanker cyberattacks, the Azure API Management flaw, a former OpenAI engineer charged over a hidden recorder, a US uranium mine cyberattack, leaked credential databases, Indian warnings on AI-assisted bank fraud, and trailer brake Bluetooth flaws. Includes a sponsor segment, which was ignored.

episodes.title: Aggressive SSH Scanning from 109.160.32.0/24; VMware VMSA-2026-0011 vCenter Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-123903) (Nov 25th 2026)
episodes.summary: Describes aggressive SSH scanning from one /24 subnet seen by honeypots, with no conclusion on its purpose, and a set of new VMware vCenter and related product vulnerabilities, with recent ones previously exploited.

episodes.title: ShinyHunters claims comeback after FBI arrests, ScreenConnect flaw hijacks MSP technicians, Azure flaw hits Norway energy firms
episodes.summary: Covers the ScreenConnect technician hijacking flaw, the Azure API Management flaw linked to Norway's energy attacks, the abandoned ASP.NET library under attack, Shiny Hunters' claimed comeback, a McDonald's Japan breach, and FCC proposals for a smart device security label.

episodes.title: AI Just Made History in the Middle of a Meltdown
episodes.summary: Covers an AI-assisted claim of a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, reactions from mathematicians, SpaceX AI problems reported by the New York Times, a new open model with looped transformers, and political fallout over NVIDIA's CEO. Largely outside the security scope.

episodes.title: Risky Business #861 -- You can’t trust AI routers
episodes.summary: Discusses HD Moore's canary token test on OpenRouter, cloud keys leaked via Docker Hub images, dozens of oil and shipping tanker hacks, a US intelligence system hit by hackers, and a CrowdStrike and Zscaler deal. The description has no further detail and the transcript was not provided, so specifics are limited.

episodes.title: SN 1106: ARTEX - Agentic AI-Driven Cyberattacks Are Happening at Scale
episodes.summary: Covers AI-driven pen testing tools like ARTEX fueling real attacks, recent outages, a DNS provider withdrawing from France, a California lawsuit against OpenAI, Synology and PHP vulnerabilities, and disclosure window changes. Full transcript not provided.

episodes.title: Rinoa Poison: The Repoisoning - SWN #636
episodes.summary: A Thanksgiving special with a guest discussing scambaiting, a conference for scambaiters and DEF CON stories. No transcript was provided, so the detail is limited to the episode description.

episodes.title: Azure API Management secrets stolen, Check Point servers hijacked | Cyber Security News Nov 24
episodes.summary: Covers the Azure API Management secret theft, Check Point management servers hijacked at 22 organizations, an ASP.NET library under exploitation, the N-able Mail Assure update, a Synology DSM critical fix, and a gift card distributor's downtime costs.

episodes.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler, Azure Secrets Stolen, Bell Breach
episodes.summary: Reports CrowdStrike's agreed acquisition of Zscaler, the Azure API Management flaw affecting Norwegian energy firms, India's warning on AI-assisted payment fraud, the N-able Mail Assure listing on CISA's known exploited list, a Bell Canada incident and NYDFS settlements with two mortgage firms.
